error_control.futility: look 1 stops when candidate minus control >= 0; not credited to alpha
error_control.r1_alpha_how: P(t > 2.0) on 89 df: 'more than 2 SE' at the fewest games R1 accepts
error_control.shape: O'Brien-Fleming: z boundary c / sqrt(information fraction)
error_control.small_sample: each z boundary becomes the Student t value of the same tail probability on games - 1 df
error_control.split: Bonferroni: the two tests' rates add to the family rate whatever their dependence

meaning.CONFIRMED: criterion 4 is met on fresh games at the family rate; R1's registered verdict stays FAIL and both are reported
meaning.NOT CONFIRMED: a better late-state win probability is NOT ESTABLISHED for coach-r1.0, with the largest gain the data do not exclude (95%) printed beside it; the question is closed for this candidate. Realism (criteria 1-3) is a separate verdict.

power.note: the development estimates were 0.0012, 0.0054 and 0.0072 nats: at those sizes this test will usually not confirm

r1_verdict: preserved; this test never changes it
statistic: per game, log loss of the home-win probability from the real state at the first snap at or inside 5:00 and 2:00 of the fourth quarter, candidate minus control, averaged over the checkpoints the game has; the mean over games, SE over games
stopping: CONFIRMED at either look ends it; futility at look 1 ends it; look 2 is final. No third look, no third test, no added season.
used_only_if: research/data/nfl_coach/read_r1.json exists and its verdict fails criterion 4 and passes the other four; otherwise this test never runs
what: confirmatory test of R1 criterion 4 (late-state win probability) on fresh games
why_these_games: every game after R1's window that R1's pinned code can play: the 2026 postseason (13 games) needs postseason overtime, which nfl_coach_eval does not pass, so it is left out
